proposal.utterance: How would you BFO-classify 'the capacity of an institution to repair itself'?

entities.label: InstitutionalSelfRepairCapacity
entities.rationale: A capacity is paradigmatically a Disposition in BFO: it is a specifically dependent continuant that inheres in a bearer (here a LegalInstitution) and is internally grounded in the bearer's structure and composition. It is not a Role (which is externally grounded) but rather an intrinsic power that can be realized in a self-repair process. 'Self-repair' denotes a possible process of institutional reform or restoration, which would be the realizing process when triggered.

entities.label: InstitutionalSelfRepairProcess
entities.rationale: The realization of the self-repair capacity is a Process: a temporal unfolding in which the institution actually undergoes reform, correction, or restoration. Needed as the target of BFO_0000054 (realized in) from the disposition.

relations.rationale: InstitutionalSelfRepairCapacity is a subclass of Disposition, the BFO category for internally grounded capacities.
All Dispositions are Specifically Dependent Continuants; making the SDC ancestry explicit for the reasoner.
The self-repair capacity inheres in a LegalInstitution as its bearer; this is the standard SDC-to-bearer relation.
The disposition is realized in an InstitutionalSelfRepairProcess when the capacity is triggered or exercised.
InstitutionalSelfRepairProcess is a subclass of Process.
Inverse of realized-in: the process realizes the disposition.

open_questions: Should InstitutionalSelfRepairCapacity be typed as a subclass of the existing working:LegalLegitimacyCondition or working:LegalExistenceCondition, or is it orthogonal to both?
Is the bearer restricted to working:LegalInstitution, or can any material collective entity (e.g., a social movement) bear this capacity?
Should InstitutionalSelfRepairProcess be further differentiated (e.g., constitutional amendment processes vs. judicial self-correction vs. legislative revision)?
Is 'self-repair' intended normatively (the capacity the institution ought to have) or descriptively (the capacity it actually has)? This affects whether we need a normative modality annotation.
proposal.rationale_summary: BFO 2020 classifies capacities — understood as intrinsic, internally grounded powers — as Dispositions (BFO_0000016), a subtype of Specifically Dependent Continuant (BFO_0000020). A disposition inheres in exactly one bearer (here a LegalInstitution, an existing working class typed as Material Entity) and is realized in a Process when triggered. 'The capacity of an institution to repair itself' fits this mold precisely: it is not externally conferred (which would make it a Role), nor is it a static measurable quality (which would make it a Quality); it is an intrinsic, trigger-sensitive power. The realizing process — InstitutionalSelfRepairProcess — is minted as a Process subclass and linked via BFO_0000054/0000055. No existing working class (LegalLegitimacyCondition, LegalExistenceCondition, InstitutionalFunction, etc.) covers this concept exactly, so a new class InstitutionalSelfRepairCapacity is proposed.
